The outermost rainbands of Super Typhoon Champi (29W) brought sub-
severe thunderstorms across Guam and Rota as well as their adjacent 
coastal waters, warranting Flood Advisories, various short-fuse
Warnings, and Airport Weather Warnings throughout the day. Since 
then, showers have stratified and cloud tops are no longer cooling, 
but conditions remain unstable this evening. Therefore, numerous 
showers with locally heavy showers possible and isolated 
thunderstorms are forecast tonight, becoming scattered near midnight.
Isolated showers will then return for Guam and Rota Tuesday. As for 
the CNMI, scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms will become 
isolated showers near midnight and continuing through midweek as a 
ridge builds in following Champi's exit, with the exception of a 
trade-wind trough briefly entering the region Tuesday night. Gentle 
to moderate trades will return to the entire region Tuesday and 
continue through the forecast period. The zones remain split to 
account for the different headlines and shower coverage tonight, but 
may be combined during the next forecast update. As for the long- 
term, several broad troughs may travel across the region from the
east, bringing periods of scattered showers and isolated 
thunderstorms later this week. A drier regime could return early 
next week.

Marine...
Combined seas are 7 to 9 feet at Guam and Rota, and 6 to 8 feet at
Saipan and Tinian, so the Small Craft Advisory was cancelled as
winds and swells continue to diminish over the next few days. Seas
will decrease by a foot or two through Tuesday afternoon before 
increasing by the end of the forecast period. Pulses of long-period 
westerly swells will move through the region throughout the forecast 
period and a northeasterly swell will build in, hence why the sea 
state will remain fairly unchanged. Gentle to moderate trades will 
persist after tonight. Hazardous surf and a high rip current risk 
will continue along south and west facing reefs of Guam and Rota 
through tonight before dropping below 9 feet Tuesday. Elsewhere, 
there is a moderate risk of rip currents along all reefs that may
continue through the week.

Tropical Systems...
As of 200 PM ChST this afternoon, Super Typhoon Champi (29W) was 
centered near 14.3N 138.7E, or roughly 335 miles north of Yap and 410
miles west of Guam. Champi is moving westward at around 12 mph, away
from the Marianas and into the Philippine Sea. Although Champi was 
downgraded late last night, it strengthened once more to a Category 4
Super Typhoon this afternoon, with maximum sustained winds of 155 
mph. Himawari visible satellite shows a well-defined, relatively 
unobscured eye compared to its appearance this morning, with a width 
of around 20 miles across. The outer heavy rainbands and 
thunderstorms extend as far east as Guam and Rota this afternoon, and
trail far south-southwestward across Yap State within a broad 
convergent inflow band, passing between Sorol and Eauripik. This 
placed Guam and Rota in the path of heavy showers and thunderstorms 
and strong, gale-force gusts this morning, with lines of showers 
continuing to build north across Marianas coastal waters this 
afternoon. STY Champi is expected to strengthen into tonight as it 
continues west-northwest. Champi then looks to speed up slightly for
Tuesday, eventually exiting Guam's Area of Responsibility (AOR) 
around Wednesday afternoon.

For more information please refer to bulletins from the Joint
Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header WTPN32 PGTW and from the
National Weather Service under WMO header WTPQ32 PGUM.

Eastern Micronesia...
A monsoon-like trough segment remains anchored across eastern
Micronesia, cut off from Super Typhoon Champi by a surface ridge 
that extends from east of the Marianas, southward into Chuuk State.
Isolated to scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms are seen 
within the convergent northwest to west flow that extends across the
region south of the trough axis, with most of the showers seen to 
the south of Pohnpei, Kosrae, and Majuro late this afternoon. A
robust trade-wind trough extends southward to interact with the
monsoon-like trough to the northeast of Majuro, producing scattered
to numerous showers and isolated thunderstorms across the area
eastward to the Date Line. This feature looks to shift westward 
through the area over the next few days, bringing increased chances 
of showers for Majuro through midweek as models depict it forming a 
weak circulation near the northern Marshalls. However, longer range 
guidance shows little in the way of meaningful development of this 
feature. Farther west, model guidance depicts a weak disturbance 
forming near Pohnpei, which could bring periods of numerous, locally
heavy showers around Wednesday night. Kosrae will see a few periods
of low-end scattered showers over the next few days, but otherwise
will see a relatively quieter, uneventful pattern.
